task_description: Classify a financial news headline about a listed company into exactly one event category. Company names are anonymized as Company A / Company B and dates as [date] / [year]. Pick the category describing the main event of the headline for the named company. If a headline fits several categories, prefer the more specific company event over macro_sector, and anything over noise. Answer with the label only.

labels.earnings_warning: Negative company results or outlook: misses estimates, profit warning, lowered or withdrawn guidance, weak sales, dividend cut or suspension, large write-down or impairment.
labels.guidance_up: Positive company results or outlook: beats estimates, raised guidance, record results, dividend increase, new or larger share buyback.
labels.m_and_a: Mergers, acquisitions, takeover bids, divestitures, spin-offs, joint ventures, or buying/selling a major stake or business unit.
labels.legal_regulatory: Lawsuits, settlements, fines, government or regulator investigations, antitrust actions, regulatory rulings or approvals specific to the company, product recalls, strikes or labor disputes.
labels.management_change: CEO, CFO, chair or other top executive or board member appointed, departing, retiring, fired or succession announced.
labels.analyst_rating: Analyst or broker actions: upgrades, downgrades, initiations, price target changes, reiterated ratings.
labels.macro_sector: News mainly about the economy, interest rates, commodities, regulation of a whole industry, or the sector or market as a whole rather than one company event.
labels.noise: No identifiable company event: stock lists and screens, market roundups, 'stocks to watch', options or unusual volume activity, generic investing advice, promotional or opinion pieces, unrelated mentions.

fundamental_shock_definition: true if the label is one of fundamental_shock_labels: an event that can change the fair value relation between the two companies, so a spread outlier may not revert.
